memories.content: Calculate user study compensation budgets based on estimated participation burden, combining session time and preparation effort.
Compensate for required travel time in face-to-face user studies as well.
Compensate for the actual time participants spent in sessions, regardless of research modality.
Leave cash payment as an available compensation method for face-to-face studies.
If compensation equity is explained, do not require finalizing the payment method at the proposal stage.
Apply the same base hourly rate to face-to-face and remote studies if task burden is equal.
Participants judge compensation fairness based on the total burden, combining session time with required travel and preparation time.
Account in compensation for the burden of rescheduling iterations and returning for multiple formative evaluation sessions.
Compensate participants for time already invested even if a session is terminated early due to prototype errors.
The author of this proposal tends to exclude preparation burden between sessions when calculating compensation for iterative studies.
HCI reviewers find it difficult to assess result reproducibility if the system version used in the field deployment is not disclosed.
Record changes in system configurations, field procedures, and data collection tools during deployment, along with their timestamps and rationales.
The history of deployment versions and configuration changes provides necessary evidence for interpreting results from different field sites.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate operational domains: the reference concerns equitable participant compensation, while the compared frame concerns deployment documentation and reproducibility. Neither frame supplies a counterpart governing the other’s decisions, and no cross-frame conflict or unresolved ambiguity is evident.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame states a budgeting rule based on combined participation effort.
relations.summary: Compensation budgets should reflect estimated session and preparation burden.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame establishes compensation for travel burden.
relations.summary: Required travel time should be compensated in face-to-face studies.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame establishes modality-independent payment for time spent in sessions.
relations.summary: Actual session time should be compensated regardless of study modality.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame addresses retaining cash as a compensation option.
relations.summary: Cash should remain an available payment method for face-to-face studies.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame governs when the payment method must be finalized.
relations.summary: A proposal need not finalize the payment method when compensation equity is explained.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame sets a cross-modality base-rate rule.
relations.summary: Equal task burden should receive the same base hourly rate across face-to-face and remote studies.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame states how participants evaluate compensation fairness.
relations.summary: Participants assess compensation fairness using session, travel, and preparation burden together.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame addresses burdens created by iterative participation.
relations.summary: Compensation should account for rescheduling and repeated attendance in formative evaluation.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame governs compensation after error-driven early termination.
relations.summary: Participants should be paid for time already invested when prototype errors end a session early.

relations.reason: Only the reference frame records this author-specific calculation tendency.
relations.summary: The proposal author tends to omit between-session preparation burden from iterative-study compensation.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame links system-version disclosure to reproducibility review.
relations.summary: Failure to disclose the deployed system version impedes reviewers’ assessment of reproducibility.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame specifies the contents of a deployment change log.
relations.summary: Deployment changes to configurations, procedures, and collection tools should be recorded with timestamps and rationales.

relations.reason: Only the compared frame states the interpretive value of deployment histories across sites.
relations.summary: Version and configuration histories provide necessary evidence for interpreting results across field sites.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers disclosure of deployed system versions and timestamped change histories needed to assess reproducibility and interpret results across field sites.
reports.reference_only: The reference covers burden-based compensation, modality equity, payment flexibility, repeated or disrupted participation, and a tendency to omit between-session preparation.
